* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, 2 to 4 feet of inundation

possible.

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a

widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/WestPinal or call 602-771-2300.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 8:36AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The Pima County Department of Environmental Quality (PDEQ) has
issued a Dust Action Day for the Tucson Metro area until 8 PM MST
this evening.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-
10 concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
pollutant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in outdoor physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this Action Day, visit the PDEQ website at
www.pima.gov/deq or call 520-724-6885.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 16 at 4:51PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63
knots, are expected. Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64
knots or more are possible within the next 48 hours.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning Saturday night,
continuing into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if
conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that
could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically
reducing visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tropical Storm Champi (29W) continues to
move quickly toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains
subject to change. However, guidance supports a passage through
Guam coastal waters, with damaging winds moving into Tinian and
Saipan Saturday night and lasting into at least Sunday night.
Champi is expected to strengthen further today and Saturday as
it approaches, then move through the region as a typhoon Sunday
morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant sea heights
reaching as high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi.
Dangerous sea conditions may continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for tropical storm
force conditions Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions
are expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely
dangerous for any vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi
approaches the Marianas, stay in safe harbor.
